lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Here's a test for any ML platform: can you tell, in under a minute, who is holding the GPU right now? If not, Antoine says you don't have a production platform, you have a shared SSH host with extra steps.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Ouch. Where does that come from?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A Run:ai webinar from September 2022 about running and autoscaling ML inference on AWS. Antoine watched it while deep in coursework and side projects, and these are the notes he kept for later platform work.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Why does inference matter more than training here?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Training gets the glamour, but inference pays the bills every hour the endpoint is up. The session framed it as a scheduling and capacity problem, not just a model-export problem.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: It sits on top of Kubernetes as a control plane for shared GPU clusters. Fair queues, visibility into who used what, and policies so inference doesn't get starved by training jobs, or the reverse. The dashboard shows jobs and, above all, the gap between allocated and used GPU time. That's where the money leaks.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: One logical model service with many replicas behind it, tied to signals like queue depth, latency targets or a schedule. Antoine wrote questions in the margin: cold starts when weights load from storage, GPU fragmentation capping replicas, and whether scale-down waits for in-flight requests.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The challenges slide. Low GPU utilization. Noisy neighbors, where training spikes starve inference. Slow GPU node startup. And cost attribution, because finance will ask who spent what.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: What would he do differently now?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Four things. Separate inference node pools before mixing with training. Define latency targets first, then pick the autoscaler signals. Add chargeback labels like team, model and environment on day one. And treat GPU sharing as a product decision.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: No, he says so plainly. The full write-up has the slides and the table of challenges.
